clues: He was born in Bukhara.
He travelled across the Muslim world collecting narrations.
His teachers included Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ali ibn al-Madini.
He died near Samarqand in 256 AH.
His Sahih is held to be the most authentic book after the Qur'an.
hard.explain: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari compiled al-Jami' al-Sahih, which scholars regard as the most authentic book after the Book of Allah. He died in 256 AH.

clues: He was born in Nishapur.
He was a student of al-Bukhari.
His collection is famous for its careful arrangement of narrations.
He died in 261 AH.
His Sahih is ranked second only to al-Bukhari's.
hard.explain: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj of Nishapur compiled the Sahih that, with al-Bukhari's, makes up the two Sahihs.

clues: He lived in Kufa.
He was a cloth merchant.
He refused the post of judge.
He died in 150 AH, the year al-Shafi'i was born.
His name is al-Nu'man ibn Thabit, founder of a school of fiqh.
hard.explain: Al-Nu'man ibn Thabit, known as Abu Hanifah, is the founder of the Hanafi school. He died in 150 AH.

clues: He lived and taught in Madinah.
He rarely left the city of the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Shafi'i studied under him.
He wrote one of the earliest books of hadith and fiqh.
He compiled al-Muwatta'.
hard.explain: Malik ibn Anas, the imam of Madinah, compiled al-Muwatta' and founded the Maliki school. He died in 179 AH.

clues: He was from Quraysh.
He studied under Malik in Madinah.
He lived in Makkah, Iraq and finally Egypt.
He wrote al-Risalah, the first book on usul al-fiqh.
He founded a school of fiqh named after him.
hard.explain: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i laid out the principles of jurisprudence in al-Risalah. He died in Egypt in 204 AH.

clues: He lived in Baghdad.
He studied under al-Shafi'i.
He was imprisoned and flogged during the Mihnah.
He compiled a huge Musnad of hadith.
He founded the fourth of the Sunni schools.
hard.explain: Ahmad ibn Hanbal stood firm in the Mihnah, compiled the Musnad, and is the founder of the Hanbali school. He died in 241 AH.

clues: He lived in Damascus.
He was a student of Ibn Taymiyyah.
He wrote a world history called al-Bidaya wan-Nihaya.
His tafsir explains the Qur'an by the Qur'an and then the Sunnah.
His tafsir is among the most widely read in the world.
hard.explain: Isma'il ibn Kathir of Damascus wrote Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim and al-Bidaya wan-Nihaya. He died in 774 AH.

clues: He came from the village of Nawa in Syria.
He never married and died young, aged about 45.
He wrote a famous commentary on Sahih Muslim.
He compiled Riyad as-Salihin.
His collection of forty hadith is memorised worldwide.
hard.explain: Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi compiled Riyad as-Salihin and the Forty Hadith, and commented on Sahih Muslim. He died in 676 AH.

clues: He came from Tabaristan.
He lived in Baghdad.
He wrote a great History of the Prophets and Kings.
His tafsir gathers the reports of the companions and their students.
He died in 310 AH.
hard.explain: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari wrote Jami' al-Bayan, a foundational tafsir, and the Tarikh. He died in 310 AH.

clues: He lived in Cairo.
He was a chief judge of Egypt.
He wrote Bulugh al-Maram.
He spent about 25 years on one commentary.
He wrote Fath al-Bari, the great commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari.
hard.explain: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Hajar al-Asqalani wrote Fath al-Bari on Sahih al-Bukhari and Bulugh al-Maram. He died in 852 AH.

clues: He lived in Egypt.
He worked on an earlier scholar's book.
He trimmed and edited it.
His version is the best-known early biography of the Prophet ﷺ.
His Sirah is based on the work of Ibn Ishaq.
hard.explain: Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham edited Ibn Ishaq's biography, and his Sirah became the standard early life of the Prophet ﷺ.

clues: He was an Umayyad ruler.
His great-grandfather on his mother's side was Umar ibn al-Khattab.
He ruled for only about two and a half years.
He ordered the hadith to be written down officially.
Many call him the fifth rightly guided caliph.
hard.explain: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ruled from 99 to 101 AH and was known for his justice. Al-Bukhari mentions in a chapter heading that he wrote ordering the hadith to be gathered.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Knowledge, chapter heading before hadith 100

clues: He was of Kurdish origin.
He ended the Fatimid state in Egypt.
He founded the Ayyubid dynasty.
He defeated the Crusaders at Hattin.
He took back Jerusalem in 583 AH.
hard.explain: Salah al-Din defeated the Crusaders at Hattin and restored Jerusalem to Muslim rule in 583 AH (1187 CE).

clues: She was from the tribe of Banu Sa'd.
She came to Makkah looking for a baby to nurse.
She took an orphan no one else wanted.
Her animals and household were blessed after that.
She was the Prophet's wet nurse.
hard.explain: Halimah of Banu Sa'd nursed the Prophet ﷺ in the desert. The splitting of his chest happened while he was with her people.

clues: She was from Abyssinia.
She cared for the Prophet ﷺ as a child.
She served his family from the time he was a child.
She married Zayd ibn Harithah.
She was the mother of Usamah ibn Zayd.
hard.explain: Barakah, known as Umm Ayman, was the Prophet's nurse after Aminah. She later married Zayd and bore Usamah.

clues: He was from the Khazraj of Madinah.
The Prophet's camel knelt near his house.
The Prophet ﷺ stayed with him when he first arrived.
He fought in almost every battle.
He died during the siege of Constantinople and is buried by its walls.
hard.explain: When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah he stayed in the house of Abu Ayyub. Abu Ayyub died decades later on the expedition to Constantinople.

clues: She was an early Muslim of Makkah.
She and her family were tortured in the heat.
The Prophet ﷺ told her family to be patient, for their promise was Paradise.
Abu Jahl killed her.
She was the first martyr in Islam and the mother of Ammar.
hard.explain: Sumayyah, mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to leave Islam, the first martyr in Islam.

clues: She was one of the Ansar.
She was at the second Pledge of Aqabah.
She went to Uhud to give water to the wounded.
She fought to defend the Prophet ﷺ when others scattered.
She is known as Umm Umarah.
hard.explain: Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm Umarah, defended the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud and was badly wounded.

clues: He was one of the Ansar and a poet.
He stayed behind from one expedition without an excuse.
He told the truth instead of making an excuse.
He was boycotted for fifty days until his repentance was accepted.
He was one of the three who stayed behind from Tabuk.
hard.explain: Ka'b ibn Malik told the long story of how he stayed behind from Tabuk, confessed honestly, and was forgiven. Surah At-Tawbah mentions the three who were left behind.

clues: He was one of the Ansar.
He was a poet.
He was one of the twelve leaders chosen at Aqabah.
He was the third commander at Mu'tah.
He was martyred after Zayd and Ja'far.
hard.explain: At Mu'tah, Zayd, then Ja'far, then Ibn Rawahah took the banner and were martyred one after another.

clues: He was one of the Ansar.
He was captured after the betrayal at al-Raji'.
He was sold to the Quraysh in Makkah.
He asked to pray two rak'ahs before being executed.
He began the sunnah of praying before being killed.
hard.explain: Khubayb was the first to establish the two rak'ahs prayed before execution, as Abu Hurayrah relates in Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: He came from Yemen.
He arrived in Madinah with the people of the ships at Khaybar.
He was later a governor of Basra and Kufa.
He was one of the two arbiters after Siffin.
The Prophet ﷺ said he had been given a flute of the family of Dawud.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ praised Abu Musa's beautiful recitation, saying he had been given one of the flutes of the family of Dawud.

clues: He was a Jewish scholar of Madinah.
He came to the Prophet ﷺ when he arrived in Madinah.
He asked three questions only a prophet would know.
He accepted Islam on hearing the answers.
The Prophet ﷺ gave him glad tidings of Paradise.
hard.explain: Abdullah ibn Salam put three questions to the Prophet ﷺ on his arrival in Madinah, and accepted Islam when he heard the answers.

clues: He was a leader in Madinah before the Hijrah.
He was about to be crowned when the Prophet ﷺ arrived.
He withdrew a third of the army before Uhud.
He said the more honourable would drive out the meaner.
He was the head of the hypocrites.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Munafiqun records his words, "If we return to Madinah, the more honourable will drive out the meaner." Abdullah ibn Ubayy led the hypocrites.

clues: He was from the tribe of Banu Hanifah.
He came to Madinah and wanted a share of authority.
He falsely claimed prophethood.
He was killed at the Battle of Yamamah.
He is known as "the liar".
hard.explain: Musaylimah came to Madinah demanding a share of rule. The Prophet ﷺ refused him, and he was later killed at Yamamah.

clues: He was a chief of Banu Hanifah in al-Yamamah.
He was captured and tied to a pillar of the mosque.
The Prophet ﷺ released him after three days.
He bathed and accepted Islam on his own.
He cut off the grain supply from al-Yamamah to Makkah.
hard.explain: Thumamah ibn Uthal was tied in the mosque, then freed. He accepted Islam and said no grain would reach Quraysh from al-Yamamah without the Prophet's permission.

clues: She was one of the Prophet's wives.
She was the daughter of the chief of Banu al-Mustaliq.
Her marriage led the Muslims to free many of her people.
The Prophet ﷺ taught her words of dhikr that outweigh a morning's worship.
Those words begin "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, adada khalqihi".
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ found Juwayriyah still in remembrance after the morning and taught her four phrases that outweigh it.

clues: She was one of the Prophet's wives.
Her father was a chief of Banu al-Nadir.
She was among the captives of Khaybar.
The Prophet ﷺ freed her and married her.
Her freedom was her dowry.
hard.explain: Anas relates that the Prophet ﷺ freed Safiyyah and made her freedom her dowry.

clues: She was one of the Prophet's wives.
She was an early Muslim who had migrated to Abyssinia.
He married her after Khadijah's death.
In her old age she gave her day to Aishah.
She was known for her cheerful nature.
hard.explain: Aishah relates that Sawdah gave her day and night to Aishah, seeking to please the Prophet ﷺ.

clues: It came straight after a famous battle.
It was against a Jewish tribe of Madinah.
They had broken their treaty during the siege of Madinah.
Jibril told the Prophet ﷺ not to lay down his arms yet.
The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to pray Asr only at their land.
hard.explain: After the Trench, the Prophet ﷺ said, "None of you should pray Asr except at Banu Qurayzah." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh judged their case.

clues: It was an expedition.
It happened the day after a defeat.
Only those who had fought the day before were allowed to go.
Many of them were wounded.
They pursued the Quraysh army after Uhud.
hard.explain: The Qur'an praises "those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had struck them." This was the march to Hamra al-Asad after Uhud.

clues: It was a tragedy of the Madinan period.
Seventy reciters of the Qur'an were sent to teach a tribe.
They were betrayed and killed.
The Prophet ﷺ made qunut against the killers for a month.
It is named after a well.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ sent seventy reciters, who were killed at Bi'r Ma'unah. He supplicated against the killers in the qunut for a month.

clues: It was an expedition of the Madinan period.
The ground was so rough their feet were torn.
They wrapped their feet in rags.
The prayer of fear was prayed during it.
Its name means "the one with the rags".
hard.explain: Abu Musa said their feet were cut so they wrapped them in rags, so it was called Dhat al-Riqa'. The prayer of fear was prayed on it.

clues: It happened on the return from an expedition.
A necklace was lost.
Someone was left behind and brought back by a companion.
Hypocrites spread a lie.
Allah declared Aishah innocent in Surah An-Nur.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nur was revealed about those who brought forward the lie (al-ifk) against Aishah, declaring her innocence.

clues: It is a term of hadith science.
It describes how many people narrated something.
So many narrated it at every stage that agreeing on a lie is impossible.
The Qur'an reached us this way.
It gives certain knowledge.
hard.explain: A mutawatir report is narrated by so many at every level that they could not have agreed on a falsehood. The Qur'an has come to us this way.

clues: It is a term of hadith science.
It describes a gap in the chain.
The gap is at the companion's level.
A tabi'i says, "The Prophet ﷺ said," without naming the companion.
It is a hadith the successor attributes directly to the Prophet ﷺ.
hard.explain: A mursal hadith is one where a successor (tabi'i) narrates directly from the Prophet ﷺ, leaving out the companion.

clues: It is a term of hadith science.
It describes who the words belong to.
The words stop at a companion.
It is not raised to the Prophet ﷺ.
Its name means "stopped".
hard.explain: A mawquf report is a saying or action of a companion, not attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. One raised to him is marfu'.

clues: It is a term of hadith science.
It is the worst kind of narration.
It may not be narrated except to warn about it.
Whoever lies about the Prophet ﷺ deliberately has a seat in the Fire.
It means fabricated.
hard.explain: A mawdu' hadith is a fabrication. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Whoever tells a lie against me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire."

clues: It is a term of hadith science.
Every hadith has one.
It comes after the chain.
Scholars check it for contradiction and defects too.
It is the text of the hadith itself.
hard.explain: A hadith has two parts: the isnad (chain of narrators) and the matn (the text that is narrated).

clues: It is a way of reciting the Qur'an.
It goes back to a reciter of Kufa.
It is passed down through his student.
Most printed mushafs today follow it.
It is the narration of Hafs from 'Asim.
hard.explain: The recitation of 'Asim of Kufa, as narrated by his student Hafs, is the one followed by most mushafs printed today.

clues: It is a way of reciting the Qur'an.
It goes back to the reciter of Madinah.
It is passed down through his Egyptian student.
It is widely read in North and West Africa.
It is the narration of Warsh from Nafi'.
hard.explain: Nafi' was the reciter of Madinah, and Warsh's narration of his recitation is the one most read across North and West Africa.

clues: It is a name for two surahs together.
The Prophet ﷺ said to recite them.
They will come on the Day of Resurrection like two clouds.
They will argue for their companions.
They are Al-Baqarah and Ali 'Imran.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Recite the two bright ones, al-Baqarah and Ali 'Imran, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection like two clouds."

clues: It is a single ayah.
It is in Surah Al-Baqarah.
It is the longest ayah in the Qur'an.
It tells believers to write down their contracts.
It is the verse of debt.
hard.explain: Al-Baqarah 282, the verse of debt, tells believers to write down a debt for a fixed term. It is the longest verse of the Qur'an.

clues: They are angels.
They glorify their Lord.
They ask forgiveness for the believers.
On the Day of Judgement eight of them will bear their charge.
They are the bearers of the Throne.
hard.explain: Surah Ghafir says those who bear the Throne glorify their Lord and ask forgiveness for those who believe.

clues: They are described in Surah Qaf.
One sits on the right and one on the left.
Not a word is uttered without them noting it.
They are always present and ready.
The Qur'an describes the recorder as "raqib, atid".
hard.explain: Surah Qaf says, "Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watcher, ready." The Arabic is raqib atid.

clues: It is mentioned in Surah Al-Mutaffifin.
It is connected to records of deeds.
The Qur'an asks, "And what will make you know what it is?"
It is called a written register.
The record of the wicked is in it.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mutaffifin says the record of the wicked is in Sijjin, a written register.

clues: It is mentioned in Surah Al-Mutaffifin.
It is connected to records of deeds.
Those brought near to Allah witness it.
It is called a written register.
The record of the righteous is in it.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mutaffifin says the record of the righteous is in Illiyyin, a written register witnessed by those brought near.

clues: It is a name of the Fire.
It is named in Surah Al-Humazah.
It is for the slanderer who piles up wealth.
It rises over the hearts.
Its name means "the crusher".
hard.explain: Surah Al-Humazah says the backbiter who hoards wealth will be thrown into al-Hutamah, the fire of Allah, kindled, rising over the hearts.

clues: It is a name of the Fire.
It is named in Surah Al-Muddaththir.
It leaves nothing and spares nothing.
Nineteen are over it.
The people of Paradise ask the criminals what brought them into it.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Muddaththir says, "I will drive him into Saqar... over it are nineteen."

clues: It is a station on the Day of Judgement.
It is promised to the Prophet ﷺ.
It is mentioned right after the command to pray at night.
It is linked to the great intercession.
Its name means "the praised station".
hard.explain: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to pray at night, "It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station."

clues: It is a rank in Paradise.
Only one servant of Allah will have it.
The Prophet ﷺ hoped it would be him.
We ask for it for him after the adhan.
Whoever asks for it for him will have his intercession.
hard.explain: The supplication after the adhan asks Allah to grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and the praised station. Whoever says it is promised his intercession.

clues: It is one of the major signs of the Hour.
It is mentioned in Surah An-Naml.
It will come out of the earth.
It will speak to people.
Its name means "the beast of the earth".
hard.explain: Surah An-Naml says Allah will bring forth for them a beast from the earth that will speak to them.

hard.answer: The sun rising from the west
options: The sun rising from the west
clues: It is one of the major signs of the Hour.
Everyone who sees it will believe.
Faith will no longer benefit those who did not believe before.
The door of repentance will close.
The sun will come up from the opposite side.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west, and when people see it they will all believe, but it will not help those who did not believe before.

clues: It was an animal.
It was white.
It was smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey.
Each stride reached as far as it could see.
The Prophet ﷺ rode it on the Night Journey.
hard.explain: In the Mi'raj hadith the Prophet ﷺ describes al-Buraq, a white animal between a mule and a donkey, whose stride reached the furthest point of its sight.

clues: It was an animal.
It belonged to the Prophet ﷺ.
It knelt at Hudaybiyyah and would not move.
The Prophet ﷺ said it was stopped by the One who stopped the elephant.
It was his she-camel.
hard.explain: At Hudaybiyyah al-Qaswa' knelt down. The Prophet ﷺ said she was not stubborn but was held back by the One who held back the elephant.

clues: It belonged to the Prophet ﷺ.
It was made of silver.
He had it made to seal letters to kings.
It passed to Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman.
It was engraved "Muhammad Messenger of Allah".
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ had a silver ring made and engraved "Muhammad Rasul Allah", to seal his letters.

clues: It is mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah.
It was a sign of a king's authority.
It held reassurance from Allah.
It contained relics of the families of Musa and Harun.
Angels carried it.
hard.explain: Bani Isra'il were told the sign of Talut's kingship was that the ark (tabut) would come to them, carried by angels, holding peace of reassurance and relics.

clues: It belonged to a prophet.
His brothers brought it back stained with false blood.
It was torn from behind, proving his innocence.
It was cast over a father's face.
Ya'qub's sight returned through it.
hard.explain: Yusuf's shirt appears three times in Surah Yusuf: with false blood, torn from behind, and finally restoring Ya'qub's sight.

clues: It is a kind of challenge.
It is mentioned in Surah Ali 'Imran.
It was offered to a Christian delegation from Najran.
Both sides bring their families.
They pray for Allah's curse on whoever is lying.
hard.explain: Surah Ali 'Imran says, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons... then invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars."

clues: It is a procedure in family law.
It is set out in Surah An-Nur.
A husband accuses his wife without four witnesses.
Each swears four times, then calls down a curse or wrath.
The marriage ends permanently after it.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nur sets out the oaths: the husband testifies four times by Allah and then invokes Allah's curse on himself if he lies, and the wife may do the same.

clues: It was a pre-Islamic practice.
A woman came pleading to the Prophet ﷺ about it.
Surah Al-Mujadilah was revealed about it.
A man declared his wife to be like his mother's back.
Its expiation is freeing a slave, fasting two months, or feeding sixty poor.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mujadilah condemned zihar and set its expiation: freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty needy people.
